newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN BOND CURVE STEEPENS ON DOLLAR DETENTE.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN BOND CURVE STEEPENS ON DOLLAR DETENTE.

text.p: Short Belgian government bonds (OLOs) were Friday's flavour as the dollar retreated vis a vis the mark, removing some of the market's concerns about a need for central bank action to keep inflationary pressures in check.
As the dollar dipped below 1.87 marks, interest flared up in switching down the curve. "They are swapping five (year OLOs) for two and then 10 for five," a trader said.

Dealers said the selling pressure was light, though, with most players trying to stay as flat as possible and go into the weekend with flat positions. The market would remain cautious next week ahead of U.S. inflation and retail sales data.

"With the dollar off its highs, the heat is off at the short end," a trader said. But another warned the Belgian franc had problems strengthening along with the mark "and therefore the money market problems are here to stay."
The franc continued to hover around the 20.65 level against the mark at midday on Friday.

A third trader said markets had bounced higher only after support levels were reached, pinpointing 101.72 for the Bund future. Fundamentally, he said, it was only a matter of economic indicators showing signs of imported inflation before prices would start sliding again.
